shots.line: The kid behind the door had my face. He told me I had ten seconds before Mom locked me in.
In this town, every lie makes a yellow door. Open it, and you find what the liar was hiding.
That morning I broke Mom's clock. A tiny brass key fell out. I hid it in my pocket.
Mom came running. I pointed at the cat. She didn't even look at the clock. She looked straight at the wall.
The door punched through the plaster. Mom grabbed the handle and said, whatever you hear, that's not your brother.
Two more doors turned yellow. Mom had just lied twice. I didn't even know I had a brother.
I opened mine. The kid inside held the hammer I'd hidden. He looked exactly like me, except he was shaking.
He said she'd been telling everyone he ran away. The whole time, he'd been right here, listening through the wall.
Mom stepped toward us. I felt the brass key in my pocket go hot. It fit a lock on his side of the door.
I turned it. He stumbled into the hallway, then grabbed my hand and ran. Behind us, Mom started counting down.
We made it as far as the street. I told him we were safe. I wanted so badly for it to be true.
Then he stopped running. A yellow door rose out of the road. This time, the knocking came from our side.
